quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Send and Void have no catch and no success feedback; a network failure or success is silent
evidence: app.js:24-29 and 31-35: fetch is awaited without try/catch, so offline or DNS failure rejects the handler's promise and shows nothing (console only). On success, send only increments sentCount, which is never displayed (app.js:3,28); void shows nothing on success. Traced.
failing_case: Go offline and click Send invoice: the promise rejects, no alert appears, and the user cannot tell whether the invoice went out, so they click again (see tooSoon finding). On a 200 reply the user also gets no confirmation and the lines stay in the list, so a second click re-sends the same invoice.
remediation: Wrap the fetch in try/catch, show a visible, announced status for sent, failed and offline (with cause and next step), clear or lock the lines after success, and drop or display sentCount.

title: validQuantity accepts empty, zero, negative, fractional and infinite quantities
evidence: app.js:17 passes the raw string. isNaN(""), isNaN(" "), isNaN("0"), isNaN("-5"), isNaN("1.5"), isNaN("1e999") and isNaN("0x10") are all false, so all are valid. app.js:20 then stores Number(qtyText) and line 10 adds qty*price to the total.
failing_case: Leave Quantity blank and add price 10: Number("") is 0, the line is added as `0 × 10.00`. Enter qty -5, price 100: the total becomes -500.00. Enter qty 1e999: the total shows Infinity. These lines are then sent to /api/invoices.
remediation: Validate with a pattern such as /^[1-9]\d*$/ (or Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 && Number.isFinite(n)) in the one place that parses the value, and reuse the parsed number rather than parsing twice.

title: The send throttle never arms: lastSend is never assigned, so double sends go through
evidence: lastSend is declared as 0 at guards.js:22 and nothing in guards.js or app.js writes it. Date.now() minus 0 is always far above 1000, so tooSoon() is always false. app.js:25 relies on it and has no in-flight flag or disabled button either.
failing_case: Click Send invoice twice quickly (or press Enter on the focused button twice). Two POST /api/invoices requests with the same lines go out, so the server may create two invoices.
remediation: Disable the button (or hold an in-flight flag) from click until the fetch settles, and set lastSend where the send starts. Make the server accept an idempotency key.

title: escapeHtml does not escape quotes but is used inside a double-quoted attribute
evidence: app.js:8 builds title="${escapeHtml(l.client)}" and assigns the string through innerHTML (app.js:7). The client value comes straight from the #client input (app.js:16). Only & < > are escaped, so a double quote ends the attribute. Traced, not executed.
failing_case: Enter client `" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)` with any qty and price, then Add line. The quote characters pass through unchanged, so the rendered markup is <a href="#" title="" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)">, and the script runs when the user hovers the link. A hostile client name (for example from a pasted or imported list) executes script in the billing page.
remediation: Escape " and ' as " and ' in escapeHtml, or build the list with createElement/textContent and setAttribute so no string is parsed as HTML.
fix: not offerable: unbalanced brackets or quotes

title: canVoid is inverted: every non-admin may void, a lone admin may not
evidence: Array.indexOf returns -1 when absent (truthy) and 0 when "admin" is the first role (falsy). app.js:2 sets roles to ["viewer","billing"], so indexOf is -1, the branch returns true and app.js:32 lets the click through to POST /api/invoices/void. Traced; not executed (shell denied).
failing_case: Signed-in user sam with roles ["viewer","billing"] clicks Void invoice: canVoid(user) is true and the void request is sent. A user whose roles are ["admin"] gets false and cannot void. The comment says only admins may void.
remediation: Use user.roles.includes("admin") (or indexOf(...) !== -1) and cover it with a test for admin, non-admin and empty roles. Enforce the permission on the server as well; this check lives in the browser and the user object is a client-side literal.

title: Invalid quantity or price is dropped silently: no message, no focus, no state
evidence: The handler returns with no output. index.html has no error element, and the price/qty inputs have no required or aria-invalid. Price also accepts Infinity (Number("1e999") > 0).
failing_case: Type price "12,50" (comma decimal) or "abc", press Add line: Number gives NaN, the guard returns, and nothing happens. The user sees no line and no reason, and cannot tell that the click registered. The same for an empty price.
remediation: Show an inline error per field linked by aria-describedby, set aria-invalid, move focus to the first bad field, and say what is expected ("Quantity: a whole number of 1 or more").

title: Void invoice is irreversible, has no confirm, and sends no invoice identifier
evidence: One click goes straight to POST /api/invoices/void (app.js:33) with no body, no id and no confirmation. The button sits beside Send and has the same styling (index.html:23-24, styles.css:4).
failing_case: A mis-click on Void, next to Send, voids with no prompt. Because no invoice id is sent, the server must infer which invoice to void, so a stale session could void the wrong one.
remediation: Ask for confirmation naming the invoice, send the invoice id in the request, and offer undo or a clearly separate destructive style.

title: Invoice lines live only in memory and are lost on refresh or close
evidence: lines is a module-level array, never written to storage and never restored; no pagehide/beforeunload handler exists in app.js.
failing_case: Add ten lines, accidentally refresh or close the tab: all lines are gone with no warning.
remediation: Persist lines (with a version field) to localStorage under a guarded parse, or warn on beforeunload while the draft is non-empty.

title: Client name is rendered as a link to # that does nothing useful
evidence: No click handler is attached to the list in app.js; href="#" only changes the hash and jumps to the top. The anchor adds a tab stop per line and is announced as a link. Lines also cannot be edited or removed anywhere in the UI. Traced.
failing_case: Add three lines and press Tab: focus stops on each client name, Enter jumps the page to the top and appends # to the URL. A mistaken line cannot be removed except by reloading and losing all lines.
remediation: Render the client as plain text, and add a labelled Remove button per line if the control is wanted.

quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Money is summed as floats inside render, so the total can disagree with the displayed lines
evidence: Per-line amounts use toFixed(2) on price (app.js:8) while the total sums unrounded floats and rounds once. Price accepts any number of decimals (app.js:18). The rule lives in the render function with no test. Not executed (shell denied); the 1.005 case follows from 1.005 being stored as 1.00499999999999989.
failing_case: Add two lines, qty 1, price 1.005. Each line shows 1.00, the total shows 2.01 (2.01 rounded), though the visible lines add up to 2.00. The sent payload carries the raw floats, so the server may compute a third figure.
remediation: Round the price to integer cents at the input boundary, keep money as integer minor units, and move the total into one pure, tested function used by both view and payload.

title: Re-rendering the whole list inside a live region re-announces every line on each add
evidence: app.js:7 replaces the whole list via innerHTML on every add. Without aria-atomic=false and appended nodes, assistive tech can read the full list again. Not tested with a screen reader.
failing_case: With 20 lines, adding a 21st can cause a screen reader to read all 21 lines again. The total (in an output element) is the only value that needs to be announced.
remediation: Append only the new li, or announce a short status such as "Line added, total 12.00" in a separate role=status element.
